confidence_basis: 1000 training rows and a cross-validated ROC-AUC of 0.800: real but modest discrimination. The confidence is capped at 'moderate' because the dataset's labels are rule-derived, so the metrics cannot establish clinical validity.
limitations: The dataset's labels are rule-derived rather than observed clinical outcomes, so held-out metrics measure how well the model recovers the generating rule and do not establish clinical validity.
The target is cross-sectional: the output is a disease likelihood, not a time-to-event risk estimate, and must not be presented as a 10-year risk.
Smoking status is absent from the training data, so the model cannot account for it; the rule-based scorer does, and reports an unknown smoking status differently from a confirmed non-smoker.

The extended model needs both chest pain type and ST slope. A case that supplies only one of them is scored by the weaker base model, so the reported confidence does not depend on how the case was filled in.
The dataset still has columns the API does not accept (resting ECG, maximum heart rate, exercise angina, ST depression, vessels coloured), which carry part of the label's signal.
The dataset is small relative to clinical risk models and comes from a single source population, so performance on other populations is unknown.
